+## 2026-08-12 — Requirements-to-test traceability, and a document that did not resolve (Issue #13)
+
+### What was built
+- `docs/traceability.md`: every functional and non-functional requirement
+  mapped to its implementation and to the tests that verify it, in the column
+  format given by the Build & Test guidance (slide 18).
+- `test_delete_removes_associated_sets`, closing a gap the matrix exposed.
+- Test count rises to 148 (33 engine, 35 accounts, 52 nutrition, 16 tracker,
+  12 core).
+
+### What the matrix was for
+The guidance asks for traceability from requirements through to the test cases
+that verify them. The stated purpose is auditability, but the useful effect
+was diagnostic: filling fifteen rows meant opening the code once per
+requirement and asking a question that is easy to avoid — *which test would
+fail if this requirement stopped working?*
+
+FR-13 is listed with status `Not Implemented` and a pointer to backlog item
+B-1 rather than being omitted. The guidance is explicit that unfinished work
+accompanied by a costed backlog is material for the dissertation, whereas a
+silently missing row reads as an oversight.
+
+### The finding: a document that looked complete but whose references did not resolve
+
+The first draft was well-formed — fifteen rows, consistent columns, plausible
+test names throughout. Checking it mechanically found **nine references that
+pointed at nothing**:
+
+- five test cases naming classes that do not exist in the suite
+  (`TestAdaptationEngine`, `TestWorkoutViews`, `TestSettlementViews`), or
+  methods under the wrong class;
+- three implementation references to functions that were never written
+  (`RegisterView`, `calculate_acute_chronic_loads`, `compute_daily_adaptation`);
+- and, most seriously, `engine/logic.py` did not appear anywhere in the matrix.
+  FR-8 and FR-9 are the project's central contribution and the module that
+  implements them, together with its 33 tests, had been left out entirely.
+
+A second draft misattributed `evaluate_day` and `resolve_multiplier` to
+`engine/logic.py`. They are in `nutrition/services.py`; the separation between
+the two — pure domain logic with no ORM, framework or clock dependency, and
+the orchestration layer that supplies it with data — is the architectural
+decision recorded in Design 3.7. Stating it incorrectly in the traceability
+document would have misdescribed the project's own structure.
+
+**What this changes about how the document is maintained.** A prose document
+cannot be run, so nothing tells you when it stops being true. The fix was to
+make it checkable: a short script extracts every `app.tests.Class.method`
